Lest we forget the blatant theft of the government; one corruption issue after the other.

Today, the tension arousing the public is more than sufficient. And just like other nations—they who used to look up to the militant Filipino spirit—the Filipino masses, too, have power over our own land. We should not wait for another flooding or catastrophe to strike. Lives need not be drowned in our waiting.  We are not ignorant, nor are we incapable. The time is now to rekindle and inflame the power of the people. The streets are out, and so should we.

data.raw_text:
CURLEE DISCAYA ADMITS PAYING 10–25% KICKBACKS TO DPWH OFFICIALS FOR FLOOD CONTROL PROJECTS

Pacifico "Curlee" Discaya, owner of St. Gerrard Construction, admitted before the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee on Thursday that he paid "standard operating procedure" kickbacks of 10 to 25 percent to Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials in exchange for flood control projects in Quezon City.

Discaya initially invoked his right against self-incrimination when pressed by Senate Deputy Majority Leader Risa Hontiveros to present ledgers of transactions. But under further questioning, he confirmed that his firm made cash payments once projects were awarded.

He said the money was withdrawn in bulk and delivered in paper bags, either at luxury hotels such as Shangri-La or inside DPWH offices. He admitted that contractors complied out of fear that projects could be canceled or delayed.

Hontiveros warned that such practices reveal the "floodgates of corruption," noting that taxpayers suffer threefold: through overpriced projects, persistent flooding despite supposed controls, and the repeated drafting of master plans that are ignored. She also asked the Anti-Money Laundering Council to submit reports on suspicious transactions involving DPWH and contractors.

Senate President Tito Sotto reminded Discaya that he enjoys legislative immunity while testifying and urged him to disclose details fully.

The admission came during the Senate's ongoing probe into ghost projects and anomalies in flood control programs worth billions of pesos.

Among the pieces they will perform are the protest song ‘Ang Masa,’ and ‘Kapangyarihan’ by Ben&Ben (feat. SB19). 

CAP encourages artists to take part in the Sept. 21 protest movement and use their talents to help hold corrupt government officials and their lackeys accountable.
